source_columns: X_PARDAT, X_RESREL, X_RESREL2, X_RESID, X_IDP1, X_IDP2, X_HPAR1, X_HPAR2, CHILDID, round
expression:
local({
  r <- as.numeric(round)
  resid <- as.numeric(X_RESID)
  id1 <- as.numeric(X_IDP1)
  id2 <- as.numeric(X_IDP2)
  id1[!is.na(id1) & id1 <= 0] <- NA
  id2[!is.na(id2) & id2 <= 0] <- NA
  rel1 <- if_else(!is.na(id1), as.numeric(X_HPAR1), NA_real_)
  rel2 <- if_else(!is.na(id2), as.numeric(X_HPAR2), NA_real_)
  id1 <- carry_within(id1, CHILDID, order = r)
  id2 <- carry_within(id2, CHILDID, order = r)
  rel1 <- carry_within(rel1, CHILDID, order = r)
  rel2 <- carry_within(rel2, CHILDID, order = r)
  rel <- case_when(
    !is.na(resid) & resid > 0 & resid == id1 ~ rel1,
    !is.na(resid) & resid > 0 & resid == id2 ~ rel2,
    .default = NA_real_
  )
  fall <- case_when(
    rel %in% c(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13) ~ "Mother",
    rel %in% c(2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 14) ~ "Father",
    rel %in% c(9, 10) ~ "Other carer",
    .default = "Unknown"
  )
  case_when(
    as.numeric(X_PARDAT) != 1 ~ NA_character_,
    r == 2 ~ recode_values(
      as.numeric(X_RESREL),
      c(1, 2) ~ "Mother",
      c(3, 4) ~ "Father",
      c(5, 6) ~ "Other carer",
      default = "Unknown"
    ),
    r %in% c(4, 6, 7, 8, 9) ~ recode_values(
      as.numeric(X_RESREL2),
      c(1, 2, 3) ~ "Mother",
      c(4, 5, 6) ~ "Father",
      c(7, 8) ~ "Other carer",
      default = "Unknown"
    ),
    .default = fall
  )
})
notes: Respondent's relationship to the child (X_RESREL round 2; X_RESREL2 rounds 4, 6-9): biological, other or unknown-type mother = Mother, the same for fathers = Father, non-parent relative or non-relative = Other carer. Rounds 3 and 5 release only the respondent's household roster number (X_RESID): it is matched to the roster numbers of parent 1 and parent 2 (X_IDP1, X_IDP2) and their relationship codes (X_HPAR1, X_HPAR2) from the child's earliest round with a roster, carried within child, because roster numbers identify persons (within rounds 4 and 6-9 the same match reproduces X_RESREL2 for over 99.8% of respondent mothers and fathers); a respondent who matches neither parent is Unknown. The parent interview's respondent also reported screen time. NA where the round has no parent interview (X_PARDAT = 0). The respondent is taken per round, never carried.

    as.numeric(P_BOTHER),
    as.numeric(P_APPETI),
    as.numeric(P_BLUE),
    as.numeric(P_KPMIND),
    as.numeric(P_DEPRES),

  items <- items - 1

    as.numeric(round) == 2,
    as.numeric(X_RESREL) %in% c(1, 2),
    as.numeric(X_RESREL2) %in% c(1, 2, 3)
  )
  mothers <- c(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13)

})

source_columns: P1BRTWGT, P1WEIGHP, P1WEIGHO, P1WEIGHG, P2WEIGHU, P2WEIGHP, P2WEIGHO, P2WEIGHG
expression:
local({
  unit1 <- as.numeric(P1BRTWGT)
  lb1 <- as.numeric(P1WEIGHP)
  oz1 <- as.numeric(P1WEIGHO)
  g1 <- as.numeric(P1WEIGHG)
  unit2 <- as.numeric(P2WEIGHU)
  lb2 <- as.numeric(P2WEIGHP)
  oz2 <- as.numeric(P2WEIGHO)
  g2 <- as.numeric(P2WEIGHG)
  fall <- case_when(
    unit1 == 1 & lb1 >= 0 & oz1 >= 0 ~ (lb1 * 16 + oz1) * 28.35,
    unit1 == 2 & g1 > 0 ~ g1,
    .default = NA_real_
  )
  spring <- case_when(
    unit2 == 1 & lb2 >= 0 & oz2 >= 0 ~ (lb2 * 16 + oz2) * 28.35,
    unit2 == 2 & g2 > 0 ~ g2,
    .default = NA_real_
  )
  coalesce(fall, spring)
})
notes: Parent recall: the child's birth weight in pounds and ounces ((lb x 16 + oz) x 28.35) or grams, as the parent chose (CHQ005-CHQ007 in the fall kindergarten interview; SPQ060-SPQ066 for parents first interviewed in spring); child-level columns kept on every row by the tidier. The public-use file holds no pounds value below 3 or above 10 (2.2% and 1.6% of children sit at 3 and 10 pounds, and the fall grams heap at 1,360 and 4,540), the look of a bottom and top code; those values stay at the bound. An ounces answer of don't know leaves the weight NA.
